title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Netanyahu vows to topple Tehran, and Ukraine says Russian skies aren't safe.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Thursday, September 03, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: US Missile Strike on Iranian Wedding Kills Civilians, Deepens War
stories.why_important: A US missile hit a wedding party in Kuhestak, Iran, killing at least four people, including two children. Iran calls it a war crime. Total deaths from recent US strikes now stand at 18, with 142 wounded, six months into the war. Killing civilians like this could make Iran fight harder and spread the war across the Gulf.
stories.what_overlooked: Most reports use Iranian state media for death counts. No one has independently checked the targets or the intent behind the strike.
stories.prediction: Watch for Iran to strike back or for the UN Security Council to meet on the war crime claim within 72 hours.

stories.story_title: Netanyahu Says Israel Is Working to Overthrow Iran's Government
stories.why_important: Netanyahu says all of Israel's forces are working to remove Iran's government. This is a big shift from just defense to trying to change the regime. He is also trying to unite Israel's far-right before next month's election. Meanwhile, his defense minister says Israel is ready to move Palestinians out of Gaza once the US agrees.
stories.what_overlooked: Few reports ask if trying to change Iran's government is legal, or how Israel would actually move over a million people out of Gaza.
stories.prediction: Watch for Israeli coalition talks before the election and any US response to the Gaza relocation plan.

stories.story_title: Zelensky Warns Airlines Russian Skies Are No Longer Safe
stories.why_important: Zelensky says more Ukrainian drone strikes have basically shut down Russian airspace for civilian flights. Ukraine has hit oil terminals, refineries, and air bases deep inside Russia. The UN's aviation agency is now warning airlines to be careful.
stories.what_overlooked: Few reports look at how these strikes on refineries and oil terminals could raise global oil prices or squeeze supply.
stories.prediction: Watch for airlines to change flight routes or for a formal safety warning from the UN aviation agency soon.

quick_hits.text: Nepal's flood death toll passed 1,250, with nearly 4,875 people still listed as missing.
Ebola deaths in Congo topped 3,000 as the WHO prepares to test three vaccines.
Nicolás Maduro asked a US judge to dismiss drug trafficking charges, citing head-of-state immunity.
Russia will shut Germany's Goethe-Institut centers after Berlin closed a Russian cultural center over an airport drone plot.
A UN report says global warming will breach 1.5C, with a best-case peak of 1.8C.
A Maltese court acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech in the 2017 car-bomb killing of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.
Uber will cut about 10% of its global workforce, its CEO announced.
Pakistan's Punjab province now allows secret terrorism trials with anonymous judges and no time limit.

big_number.context: Confirmed Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the outbreak keeps outpacing containment efforts.
